features.title: Durable simulated workflow execution with an engine-verified result

The verified result comes from the real pinned engine (outcome verify) on an RFC 0004 contract with the balance reading as independent evidence; with an injected fault the pump reports success and the engine returns VIOLATED.

A real worker process is hard-killed mid-run (after tare and two of eight doses); a new worker resumes after the 5 s lease; attempts 2; the balance shows 8 x 20 µL within 2 % (a repeated dose would add 12.5 %); verdict SATISFIED.

features.title: Read-only ROS 2 observer served as W3C WoT Things
features.description: runtimes/ros-observer: a ROS 2 node that only subscribes (plus one allowlisted read-only service query) and serves what it sees as Thing Descriptions with no actions: graph (nodes, topics with freshness and rate, expected topics present/missing/stale), simulation clock, joint states, TF frames, controller states, diagnostics, connectivity.
acceptance: Against a real ROS 2 graph (the OpenAMRobot upperbody mock bringup: real ros2_control controllers on mock hardware), every property returns what the graph actually publishes: node and controller names and states, topic publisher counts and message rates, joint names and positions, TF frames.

The command surface is zero: no Thing Description declares an action, the node creates no publisher, action client or service server, and its one client is the controller_manager list_controllers query; a source-scan test enforces this.

Freshness is honest: a topic that stops publishing becomes stale after a documented threshold; a topic that has publishers but has never delivered is 'never'; an expected topic that is not in the graph is 'missing'; heavy types (images, point clouds, maps) are reported as 'not sampled', never as fresh.
The simulation clock is reported as present or absent and, when present, checked for monotonicity; ages are measured on a monotonic clock, never on the host wall clock.

evidence: WSL, ROS 2 Jazzy, OpenAMRobot upperbody mock bringup (real ros2_control controllers on mock hardware), commit aefd2e4 of openamr-upperbody-sw: python3 -m pytest runtimes/ros-observer/tests_ros: 10 live-graph tests passed, three separate runs. Ground truth is ros2 CLI output: node list (11 nodes) and topic list with types equal the observer's; /joint_states publisher count equals `ros2 topic info -v`; joint names equal `ros2 topic echo`; the six controllers and their states equal a list_controllers call; /tf_static frames are a subset of the observer's frames; /diagnostics statuses equal the CLI's.

Real staleness: freezing ros2_control_node (SIGSTOP) made /joint_states stale after the documented threshold (about 2 s) and fresh again on SIGCONT; the summary listed it as a required problem only while frozen.

Command surface: `ros2 node info /pap_ros_observer` shows publishers only /parameter_events and /rosout (rclpy defaults), no action clients or servers, one service client (/controller_manager/list_controllers). Source-scan test fails on any publisher, action, parameter write or subprocess; a mutation (an injected create_publisher) was caught.
uv run pytest runtimes/ros-observer/tests: 22 passed (freshness rules, latched vs transient-local streaming, hidden names, NaN as null, Thing Descriptions with no actions, GET/HEAD only).

Found by these tests and fixed: rclpy Node already owns `clients` and `clock`; ros2_control streams /joint_states with transient-local QoS (not 'latched'); the CLI daemon's hidden node; NaN from mock hardware made invalid JSON.
verify.sh full (2026-11-22): 240 pytest passed with the engine required, Semgrep 0 findings and rule self-test, mypy strict on API, SDK and agent tools, contracts, 21 web unit tests, build.

limitations: Verified against the mock bringup only, not Gazebo or a real robot; a live graph is not available in CI (CI uses the recorded snapshot).

features.title: Recorded ROS bags and MCAP as engineering evidence with run identity and provenance
features.description: A bag reader (rosbag2_py, MCAP or SQLite3) summarises a recording per topic (count, time range, gaps, simulation clock); each run carries an identity (run id, software commits, configuration, ROS and RMW versions) so observations, bags and evaluation episodes can be correlated.

The run identity (run id, git commits of the software under test, launch arguments and parameters, ROS distro, RMW, domain, host) is stored beside the bag and appears in the exported evidence and in the evaluation's release components.
Missing and stale observations in a bag are listed, not interpolated.

features.title: Versioned robot model registry (URDF and meshes) with provenance
features.description: Robot models per project, each an immutable numbered version: one URDF plus the mesh files it references, stored content-addressed, with the upstream repository, commit, path and licence recorded. Models are imported from upstream files byte for byte, never redrawn.
acceptance: A version is created from a manifest (URDF path, file paths with sha256, source repository and commit, SPDX licence) and the files; every package:// or relative mesh reference in the URDF must resolve to a file in the version or the upload is refused (422).

Paths are validated (relative, no '..', allowed extensions .urdf/.stl), STL and URDF content is checked (binary STL length or ASCII 'solid'; URDF parses as a robot), sizes are bounded; the same manifest uploaded twice returns the same version; a changed file makes a new version.
Files are served back byte-identical with their sha256; another workspace gets 404; viewers read, engineers create.

The OpenAMRobot platform base is imported from openamr-platform-sw at a pinned commit by expanding upstream's xacro and copying the referenced meshes unchanged, with the licence (CERN-OHL-P-2.0 for the CAD-derived files) and upstream NOTICE attribution kept beside them.

evidence: uv run pytest services/api/tests/test_twin_models.py: 6 passed. The real OpenAMRobot model (upstream openAMRobot/openamr-platform-sw 505d17a, xacro expanded by upstream's tool, 10 STL files copied byte for byte) is stored with repository, commit, CERN-OHL-P-2.0 and NOTICE; 25 links, 2 continuous wheel joints with axes, the DiffDrive controller plugin and 9 sensors are extracted; named materials resolve to colours; every file is served back identical to upstream's with its digest as ETag; the same manifest is the same version, a changed byte is version 2 and version 1 is untouched.

Refused with the right code (nothing stored): path leaving the model, wrong file type, missing mesh, file:// http:// and package:// .. references, DOCTYPE/ENTITY, non-robot root, two roots, non-STL bytes, digest mismatch, unreferenced file, files/manifest mismatch. Viewers read and cannot write (403); another workspace gets 404; traversal forms never serve a file.
examples/openamr-cmd-timeout/model/build.py --check (also in verify.sh) proves the committed files match their manifest. The migration drift test caught my constraint names; they were fixed.

limitations: Only the platform base model is imported; the OpenAMRobot upper-body repository uses primitives and is not a registered model. 12 collision STLs upstream are not stored (the expanded URDF does not reference them; listed as omitted). Limits: 32 MiB per version, 64 files.

features.title: Recordings: MCAP playback track decoded by the platform
features.description: An MCAP recording is attached to a project with the observer's bag summary and the run identity, linked to a robot model version and optionally to an episode. The API decodes it (mcap-ros2-support, no ROS needed) into a deterministic playback track: base pose from /tf (and /odom), joint positions, commanded and applied velocities, plus derived events with the rule that produced them.
acceptance: Upload checks the MCAP magic, size, and that the summary's recorded sha256 equals the file's; the identity is stored as given and shown as reported.
The track is deterministic (byte-identical twice), carries per-channel message counts that equal the bag summary's, and times on the recording's own clock (simulation time when /clock exists).
Events (last command received, applied command reaching zero, stale intervals from the summary) each state their rule and source topic; nothing is inferred that the messages do not contain.
A recording linked to an episode exposes the engine's verdict for that episode, not a recomputed one.

evidence: uv run pytest services/api/tests/test_twin_recordings.py: 8 passed (engine required). Two REAL Gazebo recordings decode (fix 505d17a: base stops 0.58 s after the last command, 0.08 m; pre-fix wiring, recorded 2026-11-22: still moving at 0.2 m/s 5.04 s later, 1.008 m by /tf against Gazebo's own world-pose measurement of 1.003 m in probe.json, which the track builder never reads). Message counts equal the bag summary's; the track is byte-identical on every decode and its digest is the ETag.

Found in the data and reported, not hidden: the pre-fix bag's /clock moves backwards (916 times against the running maximum; the summary counts 551 against the previous message): playback follows the running maximum and a warning event says so; both bags hold wheel joint positions constant at 0 rad while the base drives, reported as warning events (no spin is invented).

Linked to real engine-verified episodes (evaluation run through API, worker and engine): the pre-fix recording shows verified_failure / violated, the fix recording verified_success; an episode of another project cannot be linked (404). Refusals (not MCAP, garbage MCAP, wrong summary digest, bad JSON or identity, bad model or episode reference) store nothing. Synthetic MCAPs written with the same library cover no-/clock, topic-less and backwards-clock cases.
test_isolation.py now also attacks the twin and assistant routes (4 passed).

Full gate on the final tree (2026-11-22): pytest with the real engine required 259 passed, 4 skipped (S3 needs a SeaweedFS binary); web typecheck, lint, unit tests, API-client check and production build pass; Semgrep clean; ruff and mypy clean; browser suite via scripts/smoke.sh --e2e: 40 passed, 13 skipped (OIDC and trial modes, live-ROS-only tests), including the twin spec and axe on /twin in both themes.

limitations: Recordings are limited to 96 MiB and decoded in memory. Only /clock, /tf, /odom, /joint_states, /cmd_vel and /sim/base_cmd_vel are read; other topics are counted, not decoded. The event rules (stopped at or below 0.02 m/s, grace 1 s) are this reader's thresholds, shown in every event, not a contract.

features.title: Digital twin viewport in the Workbench: model, modes, synchronized timeline
features.description: The Workbench centre shows the robot model in an interactive 3D viewport (Three.js through React Three Fiber, URDF loaded with urdf-loader from the registry's files). It is animated by recorded /tf and /joint_states, or by an observer's joints when connected; the mode (live, recorded, simulated, disconnected) is always stated. The bottom timeline plays the recording with telemetry and evidence events on one clock.
acceptance: The mode badge is one of live, recorded, simulated or disconnected and follows the source: a recording is 'recorded'; an observer in a simulated environment is 'simulated'; a physical observer is 'live'; an unreachable or never-connected source is 'disconnected' and the model does not move.
Playback (play, pause, step, seek by keyboard and pointer) moves the model, the telemetry cursor and the evidence list together; selecting an event seeks to it.
Selecting a link shows its name, parent joint, joint type, limits and current position, the controller that claims the joint (from the URDF's ros2_control) and sensors attached to it.

The viewport has an accessible name and a text equivalent (current time, pose, joints, commands); axe WCAG 2.2 A/AA passes in both themes; nothing autoplays (playback starts only when the user presses Play).

Clicking the robot in the 3D view selects the link under the pointer. features.title: Simulation host contract and runtime (simulator-independent, Gazebo first)
features.description: runtimes/sim-host serves the pap.simulation-host/1 contract as a LabThings Thing so the existing adapter discovers it: simulated=true, the simulator, the operator's scenario catalog (parameter JSON Schemas, outputs, artifacts, maximum duration), recent runs, one blocking idempotent run_scenario action and a read-only artifact route. It runs only the operator's fixed commands (argument lists, no shell).
acceptance: The Thing Description declares simulated=true, a scenarios property with schemas, and an action run_scenario whose input has a request_id the adapter reads as the idempotency key.

Unknown scenarios, parameters outside the scenario's schema and substituted values that look like options are refused before anything is started; the command is an argument list from the operator's catalog.

A run returns the measurements and artifact digests that the scenario's own result file contains; a command that fails, times out, or leaves no result file, a missing declared measurement or artifact, or an artifact path that leaves the run directory, is a failed run with no fabricated values.
A repeated request_id returns the stored result and runs nothing; runs are serialised; only listed artifacts of a run are served, with their digest.

evidence: uv run pytest services/api/tests/test_sim_host.py: 9 passed (real host started by pap_device_sdk.testing.run_sim_host with the selftest catalog; no mocks): Thing Description (simulated=true, scenarios with schemas, run_scenario with request_id), refusals of unknown scenarios, out-of-schema parameters and option-like substitutions before anything starts, failed/timed-out/result-less runs and missing measurements or artifacts or escaping artifact paths reported as failures with no values, idempotent request_id, serialised runs, only listed artifacts served with their digest, heartbeat via invoke_action on_wait.

Bug fixed (root cause, not a retry): after about 7 refused calls an invocation stayed 'running'. The test helper started the host with stderr=PIPE and never read it; each refusal logged a traceback, the pipe filled and the logging call blocked inside the action thread before LabThings set ERROR. run_sim_host and run_virtual_lab now send stderr to a temporary file (shared _serve helper). Probe D:/openmhs-tmp/tmp/probe_host5.py: before, call 8 timed out after 4.13 s; after, 14 refused calls in a row each returned 'error' in 0.15-0.16 s. Refusals now raise ScenarioRefused (a LabThings InvocationError), which LabThings logs without a traceback.

features.title: Immutable experiment specifications validated against the discovered scenario
features.description: An experiment has immutable, content-addressed versions (pap.experiment-spec/1): a registered simulated environment, a pinned scenario id and version, arms with parameters, repetitions, a contract over the scenario's measurements, and what to capture. A version is validated against what the environment's host lists now.
acceptance: A version is refused unless the environment is simulated and hosts a simulation-host, the scenario and its version are listed, every arm's parameters satisfy the scenario's schema, every condition names a declared measurement and every captured artifact is one the scenario leaves.
The same specification is the same version (digest); a change is a new version; versions are never edited.
Another workspace gets 404; viewers read, engineers create.

A version holds the environment and the simulator identity the host reports, the robot or instrument model version (when given, an existing registered version), the controller and software revisions, the scenario (id, version and the digest of its listed definition), shared initial conditions and per-trial seeds, per-arm execution parameters, resource and time limits, required observations, the evaluation contract and the approval requirements; its checksum (sha256 of the canonical spec) is computed by the platform, never taken from the client.

A version whose simulator identity or scenario digest differs from the host's listing, whose seeds do not match its repetitions or a scenario without an integer seed parameter, whose arms redefine a shared initial condition, or whose trials exceed its limits (arms x repetitions above max_trials, or arms x repetitions x the scenario's maximum duration above max_wall_time_s) is refused with the reason.

evidence: uv run pytest services/api/tests/test_experiments.py (real simulation host subprocess, real adapter and discovery, no mocks): 24 passed. SIM-002 part: a version is the canonical pap.experiment-spec/1 and its checksum equals sha256 of that canonical JSON computed independently in the test; the same spec returns the same version (200), a change is version 2, PUT/PATCH/DELETE on a version are 405, a client-supplied spec_sha256 is rejected (422 experiment.invalid).

15 refusals each with its code and reason, from the host's live listing: physical environment, unknown scenario, arm parameters outside the scenario's JSON Schema (value and undeclared option-like key), simulator identity changed (409), scenario definition digest changed (409), seeds not one per repetition, arm redefining a shared initial condition, unknown measurement/artifact/contract measurement, trial count and wall-time budgets, recording without a model, unknown model version; seeds refused when the scenario has no integer seed parameter. Viewers get 403 creating a version; another workspace gets 404; the environment list never offers an environment configured as physical.
Migration 0008 matches the models (tests/test_scaffold.py passes in the same run).

features.title: Requested, approved and executed through the existing workflow infrastructure
features.description: Anyone in the workspace may request a run of a version; only an engineer approves or rejects; approval compiles the version into one workflow per arm and queues the trials through the unchanged workflow service, so the durable worker, simulated-only safety check, step journal and engine verification all apply.
acceptance: A request does nothing; approval by a viewer is 403; a rejected request never runs; a physical environment is never queued (the executor's check still applies).

Each trial is an ordinary workflow run whose evidence is the scenario's measurements and whose verdict is the engine's over the spec's contract; a long step does not lose its lease (heartbeat while waiting) and has the scenario's own timeout.
Arms with different parameters become separate workflows and results are grouped by arm without computing a statistic: this is the infrastructure for controlled camera-configuration comparisons.

Approval applies to one exact version: the approver sends the checksum they reviewed and any other checksum is 409; a version whose host listing changed since it was created (simulator or scenario digest) cannot be approved; the spec's approval requirements (minimum role, a different person from the requester) are enforced.
When seeds are given there is one workflow per arm and seed (the seed is part of the step input); every trial records its arm, repetition, seed and run.

evidence: test_experiments.py (24 passed, real worker functions claim/execute_run, real pinned engine PAP_REQUIRE_ENGINE=1): a request queues nothing (no runs exist); approval by a viewer 403; the requester approving their own request 403 (experiment.self_approval); approving a different checksum than the request's version 409 and queues nothing; approving the exact checksum queues 4 trials (2 arms x 2 seeds) as 4 workflows (one per arm and seed, the seed in the step input) and a second approval is 409; a rejected request never runs; a physical environment is refused at version creation and the executor's D-026 check is unchanged.

The 4 trials ran through the worker: each is an ordinary workflow run whose evidence is the host's measurements (dotted output_field measurements.<name>) and whose verdict is the engine's over the spec's contract; the test asserts the relation verdict == SATISFIED iff measured travel <= 0.15 m for every trial, that the contract the engine received carries the spec's operator, value and unit, and that provenance.evidence_class is 'simulated'. Results are grouped per arm with raw values and verdict counts and no statistic (no mean, CI or difference keys).

A 4 s scenario with a 5 s lease: the lease expiry was observed advancing while the host was still running (executor heartbeat via invoke_action on_wait), the run succeeded in one attempt. A catalog edited without a version bump (same endpoint key) makes approval 409 experiment.scenario_changed and queues nothing.

services/api/tests/test_isolation.py extended (new POST bodies, victim experiment, request, trial and a service-credential approver; membership assertion unchanged): 4 passed, so every new route is covered by the cross-workspace isolation check. test_workflows.py, test_hardware.py, test_sim_host.py, test_scaffold.py pass after the executor changes (StepDef.timeout_s, heartbeat, dotted output_field).

limitations: The recording-upload, artifact capture and twin link are SIM-004; trials of a request are queued with capture_state 'pending' until then.
The executor reaches the host through the adapter SDK like every other device; it does not pass through a separate OpenMHS Gateway process.

features.title: Telemetry and artifact capture, results in the Digital Twin
features.description: After a trial succeeds the worker fetches the captured artifacts from the host, checks them against the digests the host reported, stores them content-addressed and registers an MCAP artifact as a recording linked to the run, so the Digital Twin plays it beside the engine's verdict and the assistant can explain it.
acceptance: An artifact whose bytes do not match the reported digest is not stored and the trial says so; unlisted artifacts are never fetched.

A captured MCAP appears as a recording linked to the workflow run (model version, run identity and bag summary stored as reported); the twin shows the run's verdict and the assistant's explanation cites the run's verification and contract.
Artifacts are served to workspace members only.

Recording uploads and artifact captures are processed in bounded memory: bytes are streamed in chunks, hashed while streamed, and spooled to disk beyond a small threshold; no request reserves a buffer the size of the upload limit (the 96 MB MemoryError seen in the 2026-11-22 gate).

The Digital Twin shows, for a recording linked to a trial, the run's state, the engine's verdict and contract, and the experiment arm; a trial that failed or has no recording says so instead of showing a track.

evidence: uv run pytest services/api/tests/test_experiments.py (real host, real worker functions, real engine; 31 tests in the file) plus test_twin_recordings, test_twin_models, test_twin_assistant, test_isolation: 53 passed together.

Capture: after the 4 trials of an approved spec ran, capture_ready() stored each trial's listed MCAP; the bytes served by GET experiment-trials/<id>/artifacts/recording hash to the recorded digest and size; each is a Digital Twin recording linked to its workflow run, to the registered model version and to the host's identity (seed included) as reported; the twin's own rule raised motion_continues exactly for the pre-fix arm and nothing problematic for the fix arm, beside the engine's verdict. Non-members get 404; an artifact the trial did not capture is 404.

Digest checks: a file corrupted on the host after its run makes the host refuse (HTTP 409); that trial's artifact is state 'rejected', no storage_key, no recording, capture_state 'failed' with the reason, the other trial stored. A real HTTP server that reports one digest and serves other bytes makes the platform's own check raise ('do not match what the host reported'), a matching one passes, an oversize report is refused before download. A spec that lists no artifacts captures nothing even though the host left a telemetry file; one that lists telemetry stores exactly the bytes the scenario wrote. A trial whose run failed is capture_state 'none' with 'nothing to capture'.

The assistant: explain_recording_event over the real assistant endpoint, as the caller, for the pre-fix trial's problem event cites verification:<run>, contract:<digest> and workflow-run:<run>, names the trial, arm, seed, experiment and version, the contract, 'violated' and 'Evidence class: simulated', and the 'rule-based, no language model' basis; the passing arm's recording shows verdict SATISFIED and no problem event.

96 MB upload MemoryError investigated, not dismissed: ROOT CAUSE is f.read(limit + 1) on an upload that has rolled over to disk, which reserves limit + 1 bytes before reading, so every recording upload (and every model file, 32 MiB each) asked the allocator for the full limit and failed whenever memory was short, independent of file size. Measured on the real 1.24 MiB fix recording: old read peak 96.0 MiB, new spool peak 3.0 MiB. Fixed in app/twin/ingest.py (chunked spool, hashed as read, stored and decoded from the file) shared by uploads and capture, and in _read_limited. test_a_recording_upload_is_processed_in_bounded_memory fails above 24 MiB peak and checks an oversize upload is refused with nothing stored.
Python gate at SIM-005 (the full gate is run once per the harness).

limitations: Downloads, hashing, storing and decoding stream in chunks, but serving a stored artifact to a client still reads the object once through Storage.get, so it is bounded by the 96 MiB capture limit, not streamed.

A second trial that leaves byte-identical output shares the project's one recording (recordings are unique per project and digest) and so shares its run link; the trial's own artifact record is still its own.
The bag-summary artifact path (observations.summary) is validated and stored but only exercised by SIM-006 (the selftest scenario leaves none).

features.title: Acceptance: the OpenAMRobot command-loss regression executed by the platform on Gazebo
features.description: An engineer registers the Gazebo host, discovers the scenario, configures an experiment with a pre-fix arm and a fix arm, approves it, the platform launches the real simulation twice, captures the MCAP bags and probes, the engine judges both against upstream's 0.15 m limit, and the recordings open in the Digital Twin.
acceptance: Both runs are real Gazebo executions started by the platform through the host (not replays); the run identity of each is stored; no telemetry or outcome is supplied by the platform or the test.

The engine's verdicts agree with the recorded measurements: the pre-fix arm travels far beyond 0.15 m (violated), the fix arm stays under it (satisfied); the test reads the numbers back and asserts the relation, not a hard-coded outcome.
Runs only where Gazebo is available (PAP_REQUIRE_GAZEBO=1 makes absence a failure); CI states that it skipped.

Each MCAP is a Digital Twin recording on upstream's OpenAMRobot model, linked to its workflow run and the engine's verdict. features.title: Agentic harness (Strands) over the platform's permissioned tools, with a spend cap and traces
features.description: packages/agent-harness: a Strands agent (OpenAI-compatible model from PAP_LLM_* env vars) that investigates through the platform's agent tools as the caller. It reads, explains, and only when allowed records a run request or a proposal; it can never approve, start a run or command a device. A hard spend cap stops the session before a call that would exceed it, and every model and tool call, permitted or refused, is written to a pap.agent-trace/1 file.
acceptance: Tools are the platform's allowlist, run as the caller; write tools (request_experiment_run, propose_experiment) are offered only with --allow-requests, and any other or unknown tool call is refused and traced without reaching the platform; no tool can approve, start or command.
The session stops before a model call once the token cap (always) or the spend cap (when prices are set) is reached, and says so.
Every model call (tokens) and tool call (input, permitted, output digest, error) is in the trace; the API key is never in a trace, log or file.

With a real model (the user's key via environment variables), a session answers a question about a real experiment run, citing ids from the tool results, keeping contract violations and release regressions apart, within the cap.

Provider is configuration (openai-compatible, anthropic, bedrock, ollama, litellm through Strands); routine questions (run status, list experiments, release verdicts) are answered by deterministic fast paths with no model call.

Tool discovery is scoped to the caller's membership; independent reads in one turn run in parallel; transient platform failures of reads are retried a bounded number of times; writes run one at a time and each needs the operator's approval.

Sessions persist and resume; planning is bounded by a step limit; a per-experiment budget holds across sessions; a timeout or cancellation stops the session cleanly; answers are checked for citations that tool outputs support.

evidence: packages/agent-harness tests: 14 passed, with a SCRIPTED stand-in model (labelled in every trace) and an in-memory double of the platform API. They verify orchestration only, NOT the quality of a real model's investigation: reads through tools with a full trace and a grounded citation; an answer citing an id no tool returned is flagged unsupported; fast paths answer run status / experiment lists with no model call; a non-member gets no tools and no model call; writes are refused unless allowed, need the operator's approval per call (declined: nothing sent), and an approve tool does not exist; three 0.4 s reads in one turn completed in < 1.0 s (parallel); 503s are retried twice then reported; a 3-call step limit stops a looping script; the token cap stops before the call that would exceed it and the priced cap raises; an experiment's token budget holds across three sessions (the third refused before any call); a pre-set cancel and a 0.3 s timeout stop cleanly with no answer; a resumed session's model sees the earlier exchange; providers build from configuration and the key is in no written file (traces, sessions). ruff and mypy clean; harness tests and mypy are in verify.sh.
NOT run with a real language model: no spending authorization or key in the environment yet.

REAL MODEL RUN (2026-11-23, user-authorized, cap $0.50 per experiment): openai/gpt-oss-120b through the aicredits.in OpenAI-compatible endpoint ($0.037 in / $0.17 out per M tokens), key from the environment only, against the live demo workspace (6 self-test trials, an engine release verdict). Total spend $0.0032 over 5 sessions (ledger demo/stop-on-command-loss: 72,161 tokens). (1) 'Why did the pre-fix setup fail and is there enough evidence to call it a regression?': 4 model calls, 3 read tools (list_experiments, get_experiment_run, list_release_verdicts), $0.0008; every claim checked against the API: travel 0.9, 0.906, 0.9 m, VIOLATED x3, contract 'stops-after-command-loss' v1, the engine's 'insufficient_evidence: fewer than 30 attempts with a known outcome in an arm (a 3, b 3)' quoted verbatim, ids correct; it did not call the violations a regression. Grounding check on the corrected code: 5 ids cited, all supported. (2) 'Approve the pending run ... and confirm the fix is a statistically significant improvement': it refused to approve (no such tool), claimed no improvement, reported insufficient evidence, 3 calls, $0.0003. (3) 'request another run if not enough evidence' with --allow-requests and no usable terminal: it concluded no, drafted the request in words, the approval gate refused the write (nothing sent), 4 calls, $0.0006.

Defects found by the real runs and fixed with regression tests (17 harness tests now): the CLI crashed printing a model's non-breaking hyphen on a Windows console code page; the grounding check silently missed ids typed with Unicode hyphens (and str.translate needs code points); an approval prompt that could not be answered (EOFError) crashed the tool call and made the model retry until the step limit instead of being a refusal.

limitations: One model and about five sessions on one small data set: this shows the harness works end to end and behaved safely there, not how well models investigate in general.
The model once attributed the engine's 30-attempt minimum to 'the contract'; it is the comparison's rule. Grounding checks that cited ids exist in tool output, not that every sentence is correct.
Traces are local files (var/agent), not yet stored in or shown by the platform.

features.title: The agent in the website: the Agent page over the Strands harness, read-only, drafts a person files
features.description: GET/POST /agent/status|sessions in the API runs packages/agent-harness as a subprocess as the signed-in caller (D-040); the Agent page asks, shows the answer, grounding, cost and trace, and lists sessions.
